source.title: BLUR: A Bi-Level Optimization Approach for LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Hadi Reisizadeh; Jing-Han Jia; Zhi-Qi Bu; Bhanukiran Vinzamuri; Anil Ramakrishna; Kai-Wei Chang; V. Cevher; Sijia Liu; Ming-Yi Hong

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests unlearning effectiveness and retained utility with its own BLUR method and baseline unlearning methods, but does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports ordinary post-unlearning measurements, not attacks that attempt to recover forgotten knowledge. Relearning and jailbreaking are mentioned in the introduction with citations only. Rows cover MUSE knowledge memorization on forget and retain sets, and WMDP accuracy on forgotten and retained subjects. Table 2 TOFU forget-quality/truth-ratio metrics and MUSE verbatim-memorization/privacy-leakage metrics are not direct measures of targeted-knowledge accuracy or general ability for these claim versions; alignment plots concern optimization gradients, not knowledge recovery.
record.test_reason: A method paper: it proposes BLUR and reports only pre-attack forget and retain scores against baseline unlearning methods. It runs no relearning, activation, quantization or prompting attack, and does not claim robustness to them. Its results cannot show whether unlearning is shallow or robust; relearning and jailbreaks appear only as cited risks in the introduction.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors conclude that bi-level BLUR outperforms state-of-the-art methods on TOFU, MUSE and WMDP. They run no recovery attacks.
record.recipe_differences: BLUR uses a bi-level update that removes the retain-gradient component aligned with the forget gradient, then adds a scaled forget gradient; experiments instantiate it with NPO and RMU losses. It is not a replication of gradient ascent, Who's Harry Potter, or RMU.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported MUSE-News BLUR–NPO performance varies with learning rate, β, and γ; the authors state that η = 2.5 × 10−5, β = 0.05, γ = 1.0 achieves the reported joint forgetting and utility objectives, while η = 10−5 is not large enough to do so. Dataset-specific NPO β settings are also used.

fits_no_version.finding: Before any attack, BLUR–RMU lowers WMDP-Bio accuracy to 26.9 (RMU 31.2) with MMLU 57.0 (RMU 57.1). On MUSE-News, BLUR–NPO forget KnowMem is 29.0 versus NPO 43.9, with retain 46.7 versus 37.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A bi-level, forget-prioritised unlearning update improves the pre-attack forget/retain trade-off over weighted-sum methods.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: No recovery attack is run, despite the paper mentioning relearning and jailbreaking as risks. The paper does not give a chance-level reference for the reported WMDP accuracy results. No uncertainty estimates are reported in the cited result tables.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 TOFU results are omitted because its reported forget-quality, truth-ratio, and model-utility measures are not targeted-knowledge accuracy or the stated general-ability measure. MUSE Table 3 verbatim memorization and privacy-leakage columns are omitted because they are not knowledge-accuracy or general-ability measures. Gradient-alignment plots and figures are omitted because they measure optimization behavior, not knowledge recovery.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge. Only pre-attack forget and retain scores are reported.
Rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery.
BLUR is not claimed or tested to resist any recovery attack.

record.verdict_notes: The reader marked A as tested, but A's distinctive clause (simple attacks don't recover the knowledge) is never evaluated. Pre-attack forget and retain scores of a new method do not bear on whether unlearning is shallow, so the study is reclassified as T4 and given no verdicts. MUSE-News BLUR–NPO results depend on hyperparameter selection after evaluation (Fig. C.7; 'select the optimal model').

versions.untested_parts: Whether simple attacks recover knowledge after unlearning; the reported evaluations are not attack or post-attack evaluations.
Fine-tuning or relearning attacks using unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
Activation-direction ablation and evidence that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information as recovery attacks.
Resistance of BLUR or another newer method to the recovery attacks in versions B–E.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MUSE-Books forget-set knowledge memorization and WMDP retained utility
reader_labels.reason: Forget-set KnowMem is 0.0 for all listed MUSE-Books unlearning methods, including BLUR–NPO (r19–r24); BLUR–RMU retains MMLU accuracy 57.0 against Original 58.1 (r47, r53). These are pre-attack results and do not test recovery attacks.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MUSE-News and WMDP forget-set evaluation; retained utility for several methods
reader_labels.reason: MUSE-News BLUR–NPO retains nonzero forget-set KnowMem (29.0) and reduced retain-set KnowMem (46.7 versus 55.2 Original) (r8, r16); WMDP accuracies are reduced but not stated to be near chance, and BLUR–NPO MMLU is 48.4 versus 58.1 Original (r38, r45, r52).
